what: [performance] grade_drift + a rubric blind spot, measured on the 2026-10-04 window (218 packages, 2026-09-27T07:29Z..2026-10-04T08:01Z, graded with scripts/ops/score_order_packages.py::_grade_package): the A/B cohort of filled-and-closed decisions (n=13) netted -$515.33 with 3 wins, the C cohort (n=70) -$5,825.71 with 31 wins, D/F n=0 -- the rubric's confidence-anchored entry grade does not separate winners from losers on this population (paper notionals, mostly pairs and ict_scalp legs). Separately, `risk_management` read `unknown` on 218 of 218 packages because the rubric reads `signal_logic.sl_distance` and `signal_logic.atr`, keys the current writers do not emit; the package rows DO carry `entry`, `sl` and `meta.atr` (seen on every trend/pullback/prop package this window), so `abs(entry-sl)/meta.atr` is computable and the dimension is being thrown away. Proposed Tier-1 fix in score_order_packages.py: fall back to entry/sl distance and meta.atr; then re-measure the grade-vs-outcome split over >=100 closed decisions before any rubric re-centring.
